# Compile an action video

Compile a promo video package — a short promo, a longer showreel and highlight clips — from captured gameplay, selecting exciting moments from recorded on-screen action-intensity peaks, guaranteeing weapons/pickups/enemies coverage, and compiling the cuts with ffmpeg at full game-native 960×540 resolution.

## Problem statement

Captured gameplay videos and per-run **on-screen action intensity** records (`.action.jsonl`) already exist, but no promo material has been assembled from them. The project needs a compelling promo video package that shows a wide range of gameplay features — weapons, pickups, enemies — at an attention-grabbing pace, produced reproducibly from the existing capture pipeline.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants showcase material (promo, showreel, individual highlight clips) to demonstrate the game's variety and pace without manual screen recording or hand-editing.
- **Secondary — prospective players / viewers.** The audience of the promo: they should see dense, exciting action within seconds (hook) and a representative spread of gameplay features.

**User stories:**

- As the maintainer, I can run one command that compiles my captured footage into a short promo, a long showreel and highlight clips, so I can share the game attractively.
- As the maintainer, I can trust that the exciting moments are chosen from recorded action-intensity peaks, so the edits feature real on-screen action rather than idle segments.
- As the maintainer, I can see which features (weapons, pickups, enemies) each clip shows, so the promo covers the whole game.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deliverables at full game-native resolution.** The work produces, written under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree: (a) a single compiled promo WebM of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (>2 min), and (c) several short highlight clips — all WebM (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback) at the game's **full native 960×540 resolution** (the game renders natively at 960×540: `src/core/constants.ts`), each carrying the game's own SFX audio track.
- **AC2 — Automated action-intensity peak selection.** The editing source pool and edit points are driven by the recorded per-run action-intensity series: peak windows (`burstiness ≥ 0.15` and/or `intensity ≥ 0.7`, merged within a 1.0 s gap, with lead/tail padding) as implemented by the existing pure helper (`src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts`) and the highlight recipe in `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5. Each selected segment is verifiable: a selection manifest lists source WebM, `.action.jsonl`, mapped video timestamps, and the intensity values that motivated the pick.
- **AC3 — Feature coverage (editorial pass).** The compiled promo and showreel visibly demonstrate a **wide range of gameplay features — weapons, pickups, enemies** (a boss segment if footage is available). A **coverage manifest** accompanies the deliverables listing, per feature, which clip and timestamp ranges show it; all three feature categories are represented.
- **AC4 — Attention-grabbing pace.** The promo opens with action (no dead air in the first ~5 s) and cuts on peaks — verified by measured criteria: the promo's sampled non-black frame ratio stays high and its average recorded intensity is at or above the documented reference band, with the per-clip intensities printed in the manifest. Editing judgment (cut cadence, ordering) is specified in the compile script's editorial config so pace is intentional and reproducible, not accidental.
- **AC5 — Reproducible, committed compile pipeline.** A committed editor script (e.g. `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` + an `npm run compile:promo` script) drives the compilation **deterministically via ffmpeg** (installed on the host, per producer decision): trim, reorder, join and mux the source clips without hand-editing. The script (`--help`) documents inputs/outputs and prerequisites, fails with clear errors when ffmpeg or source footage is missing, and its pure parts (manifest/selection logic) are unit-tested hermetically.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation.** The pure selection/planning logic of the compile script has hermetic unit tests; the delivered video files are validated (decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio track present, correct resolution) by a validation step in the pipeline.
- **AC7 — Documentation updated to reflect the changes**, including the compile pipeline, prerequisites (ffmpeg), command examples, manifest formats, and any relevant references in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` / `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Game-native resolution only (960×540)** — no 1080p upscale; the game has no native 1080p detail (producer decision Q4=A).
- **ffmpeg as the joining tool** — a host-level dependency (not currently installed); the pipeline must document and detect it. No other new system dependencies (producer decision Q5=B).
- **`capture-output/` is gitignored** — deliverables themselves are never committed; only scripts, tests, docs and (small) manifests are committed.
- **Independent of multi-scene capture tooling** — do not block on *Scripted Gameplay Videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC)*; record it as related work only (producer decision Q3=A). Fade-transition re-filming is a possible future improvement, not a requirement here.
- **No manual screen recording / hand-editing** — everything flows from the existing capture pipeline outputs (`npm run capture`, `--all-scenarios`, demo runs) and recorded action-intensity series.
- Repo conventions apply: never edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or agent-infrastructure dirs; work item referenced in commits; UK English.

## Existing state

- `npm run capture` — headless-Playwright gameplay video capture: 960×540 WebM (VP9+Opus), 60 fps, with the game's own SFX (proven 2026-10-06). Flags: `--duration`, `--tail`, `--count`, `--all-scenarios`, `--scenario <name>`, `--list-scenarios`, `--scripted`, `--headed`, `--max-duration`.
- Action-intensity metric implemented and recorded per run as `<run-id>.action.jsonl` (per-tick `rawScore`/`intensity`/`smoothed`/`burstiness`) — *Implement on-screen action intensity metric (AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2)*, done.
- Time→video join helper (`capture_started` marker + `mapTimeToVideo`) and pure highlight window selection — `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts` (+ tests), *Capture: video join + highlight selection (AH-0MUZQG13S006KL8K)*, done.
- Sample footage already in `capture-output/` (demo runs + `boss-four-hits` scenario clip).
- No ffmpeg on the host; no video-joining npm dependency.
- No promotion/compile tooling exists yet.

## Desired change

1. **Gather source footage** covering weapons, pickups and enemies at full native resolution (new `npm run capture -- --all-scenarios` and demo/full-run clips as needed).
2. **Automated highlight plan** — a script reads each source run's `.action.jsonl`, computes peak windows (reusing the documented highlight recipe), and produces an ordered edit plan (clip + in/out points) sized to the promo/showreel/clip target lengths.
3. **Editorial pass** — an editorial config guarantees feature variety (weapons, pickups, enemies each represented) and an attention-grabbing order: open on action, jump-cut across peaks, brief context shots where pacing benefits.
4. **Compile with ffmpeg** — a committed driver (`npm run compile:promo`) trims, orders, concats and muxes (audio preserved) into the three deliverables + manifests, validating outputs.
5. **Document & test** — docs for the pipeline and its prerequisites; hermetic unit tests for the pure plan/selection logic.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` (new) — ffmpeg-driven compile orchestrator: edit-plan generation, ffmpeg invocation, output validation
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` (new) — hermetic tests for the pure edit-plan/selection logic (no ffmpeg, no browser)
- `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts` (new) — type declarations (repo convention for `.mjs` scripts)
- `package.json` — `compile:promo` script entry
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts` — reference only: highlight thresholds/recipe to reuse (port the pure logic into the script where the TS helper is dev-gated/not importable from Node)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and/or `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — § pipeline documentation, ffmpeg prerequisite, manifest formats
- `capture-output/` — deliverables + manifests (gitignored, never committed)

## Related work

- *Compile an action video (this item, AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX)* — top-level promo assembly.
- *Scripted Gameplay Videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC)* — related (not a blocker): future multi-scene capture with 0.25 s fades could replace cross-scene cuts; record as `related-to`.
- *Implement on-screen action intensity metric (AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2)* — done; provides the `.action.jsonl` series.
- *Capture: video join + highlight selection (AH-0MUZQG13S006KLK8)* — done; provides the highlight recipe and time mapping.
- *Spike: automated gameplay video capture (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK)* — done; the capture pipeline producing source footage.
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5 — highlight recipe (peak thresholds, gap merge, lead/tail).
- *Screen action intensity tracking and analysis (AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN)* — done; research/decision behind the action-intensity metric (find-related).
- *SettingsScene: key-binding remapping + reset to defaults (AH-0MUA8BGE0006UAU4)* — completed, tangential (find-related).
- *Test matrix and shared fixtures for the collector-drone path (AH-0MVBMPYPB004RP0P)* — open, tangential (find-related).

## Risks & assumptions

- **ffmpeg availability (risk/mitigation):** host lacks ffmpeg; pipeline must detect its absence and fail with a clear installation message; document `apt`/`brew`/static-binary install in the docs. CI/other hosts need the same prerequisite — noted as an assumption that the operator's build hosts can install it, else this becomes a blocker to raise.
- **Native resolution ceiling (assumption):** "full resolution" = game-native 960×540; any 1080p/social-platform requirements are out of scope (follow-up item if ever needed).
- **Highlight pool quality (risk):** automated peaks may pick repetitive or visually similar moments; the editorial config + coverage manifest are the mitigation (variety, dedupe by feature, manual overrides allowed in the edit plan).
- **Scope creep (risk):** multi-scene fades (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC), 1080p output, audio editing, or a social-platform pipeline are explicitly **out of scope**; if discovered during implementation, record as new linked work items (`discovered-from:AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX`) rather than expanding this item.
- **Existing capture format assumption:** source footage is WebM (VP9+Opus) 960×540 as produced by `npm run capture`; ffmpeg trims/concat/muxes against that container (Opus audio preserved).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (Map, to producer): "Deliverable shape — (A) one compiled ~45–60 s WebM at 960×540 like existing captures / (B) longer showreel >2 min / (C) several short highlight clips?" — **ANSWERED: "All of the above but at full resolution."** Interpretation: produce all three deliverables (promo, showreel, highlight clips) at full game-native resolution — resolution clarified in Q4. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (Map, to producer): "How should exciting segments be chosen and ordered? (A) fully automatic peaks / (B) automated peaks + editorial pass for variety and pace / (C) fully manual." — **ANSWERED: B** — automated peak selection as source pool plus an editorial pass guaranteeing weapons/pickups/enemies coverage and attention-grabbing pacing. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (Map, to producer): "Relationship to multi-scene capture tooling (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC)? (A) independent / (B) dependent, wait for fades / (C) defer until tooling lands." — **ANSWERED: A** — independent; compile from existing single-scene captures; multi-scene tooling recorded as related work only. Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (Map, to producer, round 2): "The game renders natively at 960×540 — what does 'full resolution' mean? (A) game-native 960×540 / (B) 1080p upscale (needs ffmpeg or a game-resolution change)." — **ANSWERED: A** — game-native full resolution (960×540); no 1080p upscale. Source: interactive reply.
- Q5 (Map, to producer, round 2): "No ffmpeg on the host; how should clips be joined? (A) browser-based edit console re-recording via captureStream / (B) install ffmpeg, drive from a Node script / (C) defer to multi-scene tooling." — **ANSWERED: B** — install ffmpeg on the host and drive it from a committed Node script. Source: interactive reply.

Research summary: the capture pipeline (`npm run capture`) and the action-intensity series (`.action.jsonl`) are complete and sample footage already exists in `capture-output/`; the pure highlight recipe lives in `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts` and `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5. The game's native resolution is fixed at 960×540 (`src/core/constants.ts`), and ffmpeg is not installed on the host (`which ffmpeg` — none), which the operator resolved by choosing to install it.

## Plan: decomposition

Decomposed into 9 child work items covering all 8 acceptance criteria (100 % AC
coverage verified by the `tree_coverage` review). Test-first ordering: the
hermetic test suite (AH-0MVDV47VO0081VUK) is created before the pure
implementation (AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18), and the full-suite verification
(AH-0MVDV560Z002PSLT) depends on every implementation/doc child.

| # | Child | ACs covered | Depends on |
|---|-------|-------------|-----------|
| 1 | Capture: export action-intensity series + join anchor (AH-0MVDV4DMY001Z7CU) | prerequisite for AC2 | — |
| 2 | Tests: pure compile-promo edit-plan and selection (AH-0MVDV47VO0081VUK) | AC6 (test-first) | — |
| 3 | Implement: pure edit-plan and selection logic (AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18) | AC2 | 1, 2 |
| 4 | Editorial config and feature-coverage manifest (AH-0MVDV4RJ300459ZF) | AC3, AC4 | 3 |
| 5 | ffmpeg compile driver and output validation (AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ) | AC5, AC6 | 1, 3, 4 |
| 6 | Gather source footage covering weapons/pickups/enemies (AH-0MVDV4SYG008X8TY) | AC3 (source pool) | 1 |
| 7 | Produce and validate promo/showreel/highlight clips (AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4) | AC1 | 5, 6 |
| 8 | Documentation for the promo compile pipeline (AH-0MVDV53RA0079F8N) | AC7 | 5, 7 |
| 9 | Full project test suite passes (AH-0MVDV560Z002PSLT) | AC8 | 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 |

Vertical-slice note: child 1 is a capture→disk slice (series + anchor);
children 2–4 are a pure logic slice (tests → selection → editorial);
child 5 is the ffmpeg slice; child 7 is the end-to-end runtime slice
(pool → deliverable + manifests + measured pace); child 8 is the docs slice.

### Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-18** — Initial decomposition by the `plan` skill:
  - Created 9 children (see table) and wired 16 dependency edges.
  - Ran the six automated review stages and the AC-coverage review
    (100 %, `proceed`).
  - Recorded the discovered capture-side series/anchor export gap (see
    Appendix P1) and created child 1 to close it.
  - Effort/risk re-estimated by the `effort_and_risk` skill.

## Appendix: planning questions & answers

The five producer decisions Q1–Q5 recorded in the intake Appendix above remain
the authoritative answers; they were re-read (not re-asked) during planning.

- **P1 — DISCOVERY, 2026-10-18 (Map, planning session).** Repository
  investigation found that the parent's "Existing state" claim that
  per-run `<run-id>.action.jsonl` records already exist is **not yet true**:
  no `.action.jsonl` files exist in `capture-output/`, and the pure serialiser
  `src/scenes/core/actionIntensitySerialiser.ts` has **no production caller**
  (only its unit test). `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` writes only the WebM;
  telemetry (with `state.actionIntensity`) is held in the page's JSONL sink
  (`localStorage` key `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`). The §7.5 join inputs
  (`capture_started` epoch ms from `buildCaptureStartedMarker`, and the
  telemetry run-header `startedAt`) are produced in memory but not persisted
  next to the WebM.
  - **Resolution (assumption, documented for review):** close the gap by
    wiring `npm run capture` to persist `capture-output/<run-id>.action.jsonl`
    plus a join-anchor sidecar, reusing the **already-documented** §7.3 format
    and the existing pure serialiser — child *Capture: export
    action-intensity series + join anchor (AH-0MVDV4DMY001Z7CU)*. This is the
    minimal path mandated by AC2 (which requires a `.action.jsonl` per run)
    and invents no new format. Evidence: `ls capture-output/*.action.jsonl`
    (none), `git log -S serialiseActionIntensitySeries` (serialiser commit
    only), `grep -rn serialiseActionIntensitySeries src/ scripts/` (no
    production caller).
  - **OPEN QUESTION (to producer, non-blocking):** if you would prefer the
    compiler to instead derive the series from a `npm run record`
    telemetry dump (rather than having `npm run capture` write it), say so and
    child 1 will be re-scoped. Recommendation: keep the capture-side export
    (it matches docs §7.3 and keeps WebM + series co-located).
- **P2 — ASSUMPTION (Map, planning session).** The parent AC4 "documented
  reference band" for average recorded intensity is **not yet documented**
  anywhere in `docs/dev/`. Planned resolution: child 7 documents the band
  (with its calibration basis) and child 8 records it in the docs; the band is
  derived from the captured peak windows rather than fixed a priori.
  - **OPEN QUESTION (to producer, non-blocking):** do you want a specific
    minimum mean-intensity threshold (e.g. ≥ 0.4) written into the docs, or is
    a calibration-derived band recorded from the produced footage acceptable?
    Recommendation: calibration-derived band, documented with the measured
    values.
- **P3 — DECISION (Map, planning session).** Approval gate check returned
  `request_approval: false` (effort Medium, risk Medium — not Extra Large +
  High/Severe), so the plan proceeded without a producer approval pause, per
  the plan skill's gate rule.

# Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature

## Problem statement

Recording a human play session for balance statistics (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) currently
requires the operator to discover and run the `npm run record` tool (which needs a
display + Playwright), or to manually dig a multi-megabyte string out of the player's
browser `localStorage` and paste it into a file (awkward, error-prone, size-limited).
There is no way to get telemetry from **any** browser hitting the dev server. We want a
dev-mode-only, zero-effort flow: the game itself collects the run, and at the end of
the game uploads the telemetry file to the server the game is running on; the server
stores it in `recordings/` and automatically runs the human evaluation on it.

None of this must be reachable when dev mode is not enabled (production builds, static
hosting, `vite preview`/`vite build` output).

## Users

- **As a maintainer**, I want any browser playing the dev-mode game to automatically
  deliver its recorded run telemetry to the dev server and have the human evaluation
  run on it, so I can collect balance statistics without any manual export step.
- **As a player/operator in dev mode**, I want telemetry collection to be controllable
  via a game setting (on by default), so I can opt out of upload without restarting the
  server.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dev-only feature gate.** A fresh `npm run dev` game session (no special env vars)
   collected the run's telemetry by default and uploaded it at run end; the upload
   mechanism and the collection-on-by-default behaviour are unreachable in a
   production build. A dev-only enforcement test asserts no production call site /
   production bundle path can enable upload or collect-on-by-default.
2. **Setting (on by default).** A new game setting, e.g. "Share telemetry with the dev
   server (dev mode)" in `SettingsScene`, persisted in the existing settings store,
   defaults to **on**. When off, the dev game neither collects nor uploads telemetry.
   The setting is inert (ignored) in non-dev builds.
3. **Upload at end of game.** At run end (the existing `_finishRun`/run-end hook), and
   only when dev mode + setting on, the game POSTs the local JSONL sink's accumulated
   telemetry (`ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`) to the dev server the page was served from
   (same-origin fetch; no change to production telemetry/consent config). The upload
   is fire-and-forget and must not block or crash the game.
4. **Server-side receipt.** The dev server (Vite dev-only middleware, `apply: 'serve'`,
   mirroring `configCsvPlugin`) exposes an upload endpoint. On receipt it validates
   the body against the telemetry schema/recording reader, stores it in the
   `recordings/` folder using the existing `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` naming, and
   returns a confirmation. Malformed bodies are rejected (4xx) and never written.
5. **Automatic evaluation.** After a valid recording is stored, the human evaluation
   pipeline runs automatically on it (the existing `--human` path producing
   `human-balance-report.json` and companions under an `eval-output/`-style location).
   The evaluation runs asynchronously so it never blocks the game or the upload
   response; its completion/summary is logged. The full existing `npm run record` /
   `npm run evaluate -- --human` flows continue to work unchanged.
6. **Tests + docs.** Tests cover: the setting (default on, persistence, dev-only
   behaviour), the uploader (fires at run end with the sink content when dev+on,
   no-op otherwise), the server middleware (valid/invalid bodies, storage path, eval
   trigger, dev-only registration) and the dev-only enforcement scan. Docs
   (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`) describe the dev-mode
   auto-upload + automatic evaluation flow. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Dev-tooling only.** No production call site, no change to production
  telemetry/consent config (`VITE_TELEMETRY_CONSENT`, consent prompt). Production
  builds never collect or upload via this path.
- Reuse the existing telemetry framework sinks and record schema — no new recording
  mechanism, no schema divergence.
- The existing `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` local sink content is the canonical payload;
  the sink's localStorage content is left intact after upload (existing
  `npm run record` and inspection flows must keep working).
- No PII handling change: the payload is the same schema-only recording already
  written by the local dev sink.
- Same-origin upload (the page is served by the dev server), so no CORS work.
- Evaluation reuse: the shipped `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` pipeline (and its
  `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` core) is invoked as-is rather than reimplemented.

## Existing state

- `src/telemetry/` — consent-gated framework; local dev sink writes JSONL to
  `localStorage` under `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`; disabled by default (`VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`).
- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — typed `SettingsRecord` persisted under
  `ai_hell_settings` (volume, mute, bindings); settings scene reads/writes it.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_finishRun()` (≈3262) is the run-end hook that already
  calls `runTelemetry.runEnd()` and emits the dev-gated run-ended signal.
- `vite.config.ts` + `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — the established dev-only
  middleware pattern (`apply: 'serve'`, Vite plugin with HTTP endpoints); a telemetry
  upload plugin should follow it.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` / `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — `parseRecording` /
  `parseTelemetryJsonl` for validating and splitting the flat record stream.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — the `--human` evaluation pipeline
  (same-seed comparison + `human-balance-report.json` from the shared helper,
  AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN).
- `recordings/` is gitignored (dev play recordings, AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ).

## Desired change

1. New `SettingsRecord` field (e.g. `shareTelemetryDev: boolean`, default `true`),
   surfaced as a toggle in `SettingsScene`; inert unless `import.meta.env.DEV`.
2. In dev mode, when the setting is on, the game enables the local jsonl sink (the
   default dev config currently requires `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true` — this feature
   makes a stock `npm run dev` collect when the setting is on) and, at `_finishRun()`,
   POSTs the sink's JSONL content to the dev server.
3. New dev-only Vite plugin (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`, registered
   `apply: 'serve'`) exposing e.g. `POST /api/telemetry/upload`: validate → write
   `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` → trigger the human evaluation asynchronously
   (spawn `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --human <file> --out <eval-output>/uploaded/<ts>` or
   invoke the CLI core via SSR) → log the result.
4. Dev-only enforcement test (mirroring the existing human-stats scan) asserting neither
   the upload path nor the on-by-default collection is reachable from production
   sources/builds.
5. Docs update (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`).

## Key Files

- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — new setting field + default.

# Implement: pure edit-plan and selection logic in compile-promo

## Goal

Implement the pure, committed selection/planning logic of the promo compiler
(`scripts/compile-promo.mjs` + `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts`): read each
source run's `.action.jsonl`, compute highlight windows with the documented
§7.5 recipe, map to video time, and produce an ordered edit plan sized to the
three deliverable targets, emitting the **selection manifest** (AC2 of the
parent).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can run a committed script that turns my
captured runs' action-intensity series into an ordered edit plan, so the promo
is driven by measured on-screen action rather than hand-picked moments.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Series reader.** Parses `capture-output/<run-id>.action.jsonl`
  (header + one sample per line), skipping malformed/truncated lines and
  tolerating header-only files.
- **AC2 — Window selection.** Produces highlight windows matching the
  documented recipe (§7.5 thresholds `θ=0.15`, `I_hi=0.7`, `g=1.0 s`,
  `lead=1.5 s`, `tail=1.0 s`, merged + clamped) — consistent with
  `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts`.
- **AC3 — Video-time mapping.** Maps window series-times to video times using
  the persisted join anchor (capture_started / run startedAt), falling back to
  approximate mapping when the anchor is missing.
- **AC4 — Sized edit plan.** Produces an ordered edit plan sized to the three
  targets (promo ~45–60 s, showreel > 2 min, several highlight clips),
  respecting per-source duration constraints; deterministic (same inputs ⇒
  same plan).
- **AC5 — Selection manifest.** Emits the selection manifest listing, per
  selected segment: source WebM, source `.action.jsonl`, mapped video
  timestamps (in/out), and the intensity/burstiness values that motivated the
  pick.
- **AC6 — CLI contract.** `scripts/compile-promo.mjs --help` documents
  inputs, outputs and prerequisites (ffmpeg); missing source footage or series
  yields a clear, actionable error. The pure path runs **without ffmpeg**.
- **AC7 — Type declarations.** `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts` declares the
  module's public types/consts so the TS test suite type-checks (repo
  convention).
- **AC8 — Tests green.** The test-first suite (sibling item) passes.

- **Covers parent AC2:** **AC2 — Automated action-intensity peak selection.** The editing source pool and edit points are driven by the recorded per-run action-intensity series: peak windows (`burstiness ≥ 0.15` and/or `intensity ≥ 0.7`, merged within a 1.0 s gap, with lead/tail padding) as implemented by the existing pure helper (`src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts`) and the highlight recipe in `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.5. Each selected segment is verifiable: a selection manifest lists source WebM, `.action.jsonl`, mapped video timestamps, and the intensity values that motivated the pick.

## Goal

Implement the ffmpeg-driven part of the pipeline (AC1, AC5, AC6 of the
parent): trim, reorder, join and mux source clips **deterministically via
ffmpeg** into the three deliverable types (promo, showreel, highlight clips)
at game-native 960×540 with the game's own SFX audio, and validate the outputs
(decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio present, correct resolution).

**User story:** As the maintainer, one command (`npm run compile:promo`)
turns my captured footage into the promo package, and the script tells me
loudly and clearly when ffmpeg or footage is missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — ffmpeg invocation.** Trims each selected segment to its mapped in/out
  points, reorders, concatenates and muxes audio deterministically; sources are
  the WebM (VP9+Opus, or VP8 fallback) produced by `npm run capture`.
- **AC2 — Three deliverable types.** Produces (a) a single compiled promo WebM
  of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (> 2 min), (c) several short
  highlight clips — all WebM at the game's full native 960×540 resolution with
  the game's own SFX audio track.
- **AC3 — Output validation.** A validation step confirms each deliverable is
  decodable, has non-trivial non-black pixels, carries an audio track, and is
  at 960×540; validation failures are reported with actionable messages.
- **AC4 — Clear errors.** Missing ffmpeg or missing source footage yields a
  clear error with installation/runtime hints (ffmpeg install commands in
  `--help` and docs), not a stack trace.
- **AC5 — npm entry point.** `npm run compile:promo` drives the pipeline; the
  driver documents inputs, outputs and prerequisites via `--help`.
- **AC6 — Hermetic separation.** The ffmpeg-dependent path is isolated from
  the pure logic; the pure parts remain unit-tested without ffmpeg (see the
  sibling pure/test items). An optional integration smoke test is gated on
  ffmpeg presence and real or synthetic footage.

- **Covers parent AC5:** **AC5 — Reproducible, committed compile pipeline.** A committed editor script (e.g. `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` + an `npm run compile:promo` script) drives the compilation **deterministically via ffmpeg** (installed on the host, per producer decision): trim, reorder, join and mux the source clips without hand-editing. # Implement wormhole transit movement, parity and docs

## Goal

As a player I expect enemies to emerge from the wormhole and traverse to their formation
positions, so that spawning feels cinematic and diegetic rather than popping into existence.

Part of **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** (Enemies should emerge from the wormhole).

## Scope

Implement the transit movement in the shared spawn helpers and wire both scenes to use it, so the
same code runs in the game and every formation gym (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).

- Extend `SpawnState` in `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` with the spawn origin and destination
  positions; extend `startSpawnAnimation` to accept a destination (defaulting to no movement for
  callers that do not need it) and `updateSpawnAnimation` to interpolate the entity's position from
  the origin to the destination over the spawn window, reaching the destination no later than the
  end of the protection window.
- `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` — instantiate the enemy at the wave's wormhole position
  (`spawns[0].x, spawns[0].y`) and set its destination to the configured formation position
  (`spawn.x, spawn.y`). Spawn positions and timing must otherwise be unchanged.
- `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation` — the same pattern: create each entity at the formation
  base (wormhole) position and set its destination to its formation slot position.
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §2.7 to document the movement phase and its
  timing, and update the relevant Timeline/Implementation/Tests bullets.
- Preserve all existing `isSpawning` spawn-protection gates (bullets, body collision, shooting,
  mineral absorption) and the single-live `WormholeController` lifecycle.
- Verify the Diver's existing movement/animation pipeline is not disturbed during transit.
- Run the full project test suite and ensure it passes.

## Acceptance Criteria


- Each spawned enemy starts at the wormhole position and moves to its configured formation position over the spawn-protection window; the same movement behaviour is applied consistently to both PlayScene and all gym scenes that spawn enemies.
- The movement completes within the existing 3-second spawn-protection window so enemies are fully arrived before the wormhole closes and before they become collidable.
- Spawn protection is retained during transit (player bullets pass through, no shooting, no body collision, no mineral absorption) and the same movement behaviour runs in PlayScene and every gym scene that spawns enemies.
- docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md §2.7 documents the movement phase and its timing.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes.
## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — extend SpawnState and the spawn-animation helpers.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_spawnEnemy()` spawn origin + destination.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_spawnFormation()` spawn origin + destination.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §2.7 movement documentation.

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW
- AH-0MURBER4L00821RR (completed) — wormhole VFX + growth + spawn-protection gates.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: linear interpolation from the wormhole position to the formation position is the
  chosen approach; no curved path is required.
- Risk: the Diver's existing movement pipeline may conflict with spawn transit — verify and guard.
